To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the problem of on-the-fly annotation is feasible, (ii) the problem of annotating short text fragments is feasible, and (iii) the problem of using Wikipedia to enrich the semantics of a text is feasible.

(1) it is possible, and (2) it is feasible to annotate short texts with hyperlinks to Wikipedia articles, using the Wikipedia knowledge-base as the sole source of knowledge; (3) the annotation can be done efficiently, in real-time, with low memory requirements; (4) the quality of the annotation is high, as measured against a manually annotated corpus; and (5) the annotation is useful in the context of information retrieval.

TAGME is a system which can automatically augment a plain text with hyperlinks to Wikipedia entities (pages and categories).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to automatically annotate a text snippet with a set of Wikipedia pages, such that the text snippet is the most informative part of the page.

it is possible to annotate short and poorly composed text fragments with a very high accuracy, and that such annotations may be used to enhance the quality of a large class of tasks.
